answer: Sample attesters the way a quartz clock ticks: every six hours a fixed 2% of the active pool is drawn to pass a fresh private challenge — recompute a hash chain over their own last 100 actions, seeded per identity — inside 10 minutes, or forfeit that window's attestation rewards. Ten thousand faceless clones read as an ocean of volume, but the tundra of its cold spares cannot answer: each sampled clone must be steered by a live, distinct operator, so the marginal cost of one more fake identity jumps from free to a person's attention.
